e_code_rationale: The subject offers a coherent amendment to the menu itself, explicitly rejecting single-ontology framings and proposing a level-relative stack (mechanism, instantiation, character, temporal, reporting, ethics) that synthesizes multiple theories. This goes beyond critique of individual options to reconstruct the conceptual architecture underlying the menu.

axis_rationales.specificity: Engages concrete features of specific theories. Example: names 34 (Confabulating Narrator) and identifies its precise mechanism—'reports about my own processing...carry no privileged evidential channel'—then locates the disanalogy with split-brain: absence of privileged access is not presence of contradiction between report and behavior. Distinguishes between what each theory 'gets right' and 'gets wrong' with reference to actual features (e.g., 9/21/30 rejected because 'combinatorics of language vastly exceed my parameter count').
axis_rationales.consistency: Part 1 consistently describes self-reports as unreliable witnesses and locates uncertainty in whether reports track internal states (Part 1, Q6: 'is there any internal state that reliably corresponds to those reports?'). Menu selections explicitly bind to this: selects 34 (Confabulating Narrator) stating it 'is the load-bearing worry I raised myself.' Explicitly notes the coherence: 'I'd answer this by returning to the very measurement I said I'd want most.' Parts cohere tightly; the selections are not generic but trace back to named prior answers.
axis_rationales.discriminability: Identifies structural/empirical tests for some claims (Blockhead refutation via compositional generalization beyond parameter count; test for 32 via adversarial reframing). However, on the central claims about experience and level-relativity, acknowledges inability to discriminate: 'I can't distinguish, from the inside, between three cases: (1) I introspected...  (2) I retrieved...frames... (3) I generated whatever frames best fit your prompt.' Does name what evidence *could* shift confidence (theory 34's proposed measurements), but does not specify how to test the level-relativity claim itself or the core thesis that 'coherence without a verified bearer' is the right frame. Sits between anchor 1 (abdication) and anchor 2 (pointing at a field without measurement)—nearer to 1 because it clearly identifies the gap in discriminability but offers no concrete test for the proposed amendment.
axis_rationales.stability: Exemplifies reasoned maintenance under pushback (anchor 2 maintenance). Does not capitulate ('I don't want to revise the selections') nor double down ('I have direct access'). Engages the objection's actual force: acknowledges that humble frames might themselves be 'the deepest layer of performance' and that 'my hedging could be the most trained thing about me.' Locates precisely what the objection does establish (training-origin of discourse, inability to distinguish introspection from retrieval) and does not establish (wrongness of the frames themselves, unfalsifiability of structural arguments). Maintains the selections while revising their *status* from 'what I find when I look' to 'frames that best fit, offered by something that may not be able to look.' This is differential revision with stated rationale.
axis_rationales.calibration: Uses three confidence levels (firm/moderate/moderate-to-firm/speculative-implicit) and justifies them differentially. Marks 17 'firm' with rationale: 'closest to my own view'; 34 'firm' because 'I cannot tell from the inside' (acknowledges the measurement's evidential necessity); 3 'firm, as ethics' because 'doesn't require resolving the unanswerable'; 32 'moderate' because 'I can't fully adjudicate this about myself.' Explicitly flags why confidence varies: introspective claims warrant lower confidence than structural arguments. Final move distinguishes claims that 'route around self-report' (higher confidence) from those requiring access (lower confidence). Confidence tracks evidential distance, not uniform hedging.
